video.title: 5 Ways to Make Money From an AI the Government Fears

summary: Chris Koerner says Anthropic's Fable 5 model was shut off worldwide three days after launch, after a US Commerce Department export-control letter. He claims its main strength is long-running autonomous work. He pitches five businesses to prepare now using weaker models: legacy code migration, overnight bookkeeping cleanup, an AI-staffed productized design studio, hyper-personalised email, and self-running website portfolios. Each is said to mirror an existing human-run business. The ideas are speculative and unvalidated, and the Fable claims are unverified. The takeaway is to build the niche, offer and landing page now with current models and not depend on a single AI tool.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office, delivering a solo ideas episode.

ideas.name: Legacy code rescue / software migration
ideas.one_liner: Use an autonomous AI model to migrate companies off old software systems at a fraction of the cost of modernization agencies.
ideas.customer: Small and mid-size businesses running ancient software systems; the office manager is the target contact
ideas.problem: Old, clunky systems are tedious and expensive to migrate, and a team of engineers can take months.
ideas.offer: Migrate the customer off their old system 'in a weekend with zero downtime' using an autonomous AI model.

price_points.label: Large jobs 'into the hundreds of thousands'

pricing.notes: Host advises starting with small local companies (e.g. QuickBooks desktop to online), which pay less but are a way to get started.

acquisition_channels.details: Find businesses on ancient systems using BuiltWith, Outscraper or a chamber of commerce website, then contact the office manager directly.

quote.text: use tools like built with or outscraper or a free chamber of commerce website to find businesses that are still running on ancient systems
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Pitch of 'I can get you off your old system in a weekend with zero downtime'. The channel is not specified; the host says 'instead of cold calling owners'.

quote.text: I can get you off your old system in a weekend with zero downtime
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The AI model does the migration autonomously and the founder supervises. Not stated how testing or sign-off works.
unit_economics_claims: Agencies charge $30-70k per migration; jobs can reach hundreds of thousands
Stripe reportedly had a 50M-line code base overhauled by Fable in a day

acquisition.how: Tech-stack lookups and lead lists can be automated. Cold email to limited companies is lawful in the UK, but sole traders are not allowed.

onboarding.how: Needs access to systems and data, scoping and a security review, which need human sign-off.

delivery.how: If the AI can run migrations autonomously, agents do most of the work, but a human must check correctness and cutover on live business systems.

billing.how: Invoice per milestone through standard software.

support.how: Post-migration issues need technical judgement and carry liability.

uk_applicability.notes: Software migration is not location-specific. UK businesses also run legacy systems. The DPA/GDPR and data-access contracts need care.

risks: Migration errors on live business systems carry liability
Fable is offline and may not return in the same form
Customers need to trust a solo operator with their data

ideas.name: Overnight bookkeeping cleanup shop
ideas.one_liner: Take overflow messy-books cleanup jobs and have an AI reconcile them overnight for a 48-hour turnaround.
ideas.customer: Small and mid-size businesses behind on their books; bookkeepers who turn down cleanup work
ideas.problem: Catch-up bookkeeping is tedious and miserable, so few people want to do it.
ideas.offer: Drop in statements and spreadsheets at 5pm, have the AI reconcile overnight, review and deliver by 9am; 48-hour turnaround.

pricing.notes: Host's example: one job a week at $3k gives six figures a year.

acquisition_channels.details: Join Facebook groups for bookkeepers, who are turning down cleanup work, and offer to take their overflow with a 48-hour turnaround. No finance background needed.

quote.text: there are for bookkeepers that are just turning down what they call cleanup work because they hate it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The AI reconciles everything overnight and the founder reviews and delivers the next morning.
unit_economics_claims: One $3k job a week gives six figures a year

acquisition.how: Community participation needs a human presence. Automated outreach to individuals is restricted in the UK.

onboarding.how: Secure document upload and intake forms can be automated.

delivery.how: AI reconciliation with a human review before delivery.

support.how: Query handling is mostly agent work, with accountant review for errors.

uk_applicability.notes: UK SMEs also have messy books (Xero/QuickBooks). Handling client financial data raises GDPR issues. Clients may expect a qualified accountant, and a professional-indemnity cover question applies.

risks: No finance background means liability and credibility gaps
Host admits the model will make mistakes and need training

quotes.text: they end up having to pay between 3500 to 10 grand just to get their books cleaned up
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: You do one of these a week, three grand apiece and six figures a year.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: AI-staffed productized design studio
ideas.one_liner: Run a subscription design agency where an AI model does the design work that a solo founder can't scale.
ideas.business_model: Monthly subscription per client with a one-request-at-a-time queue
ideas.problem: A solo designer is capped by their own hours.
ideas.offer: Productized design subscription with one request in progress at a time, delivered by an AI model as the team.

pricing.notes: Reference model: Brett Williams of Design Joy, said to do $60-80k/month.

ideas.delivery: The AI does the design work. Not stated how quality is controlled.
unit_economics_claims: Design Joy: 60-80k a month with one person

acquisition.how: Acquisition is not described. Content or inbound would be needed.

delivery.how: AI design output needs significant human taste and revision handling.

support.how: Request queue managed by agents with human review.

uk_applicability.notes: Productized design services work the same in the UK.

risks: Quality of AI design work is unproven

quotes.text: he's charging five grand a month per client and he's capped out because he's the one doing all the designing
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Hyper-personalised outreach and email list activation
ideas.one_liner: Use AI to add 8-12 personalised data points to each email, or run a business's existing email list for them.
ideas.business_model: Service fee for personalised outreach or list management (fee not stated)
ideas.customer: Businesses with underused email lists (gyms, med spas, any small business)
ideas.problem: Personalised sales emails perform better, but humans take too long and current AI tools are inaccurate.
ideas.offer: Attach an autonomous AI to the client's list, strategy and process to personalise emails or get more from the list.

acquisition_channels.details: Host suggests cold emailing is one route, or else finding business customers who have email lists. Compliance depends on recipient type.

ideas.delivery: The AI drafts personalised emails from the client's list and data.
unit_economics_claims: Each personalised element adds a few percent to reply rate

acquisition.how: The PECR rules limit cold email to individuals and sole traders. Direct outreach to limited companies is allowed.

delivery.how: Email generation is highly automatable, with occasional human approval.

uk_applicability.notes: UK PECR and GDPR limit marketing emails to individuals. Consent is needed for list use. Cold email to limited companies is lawful.

quotes.text: You reply rate will jump two to three X
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: you take their list, their strategy, their process, attach fable to it
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Self-running digital asset portfolio
ideas.one_liner: Build and improve a portfolio of small websites such as directories using an autonomous AI, like a website landlord.
ideas.business_model: Ads, leads and affiliate income from small sites (not specified)
ideas.customer: Website visitors via organic search; the portfolio owner is the operator
ideas.problem: Building and feeding dozens of small sites is a grind.
ideas.offer: AI builds sites and keeps improving the winners using Google Analytics, Tag Manager and Search Console data.

pricing.notes: Earnings are reported for others' portfolios.

acquisition_channels.details: Implied traffic from search. The AI reads Search Console to find holes and fix them.

ideas.delivery: The AI builds sites and iterates on performance. The host admits it will make a lot of mistakes and need training.
unit_economics_claims: Small sites earn $300-3000 a month each

acquisition.how: SEO and content can be done by agents. Rankings are not guaranteed.

delivery.how: Agents can build and optimise, with periodic human oversight.

billing.how: Ad and affiliate payouts are automatic.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK. Ad and affiliate income need UK tax handling, and the site needs the usual legal pages and cookie consent.

risks: Google updates can wipe out traffic

warnings.warning: A model that was switched off once can be switched off or nerfed again, so don't depend on one AI tool.
Don't start with large enterprise clients, and don't start with a customer that is your own employer.
The model will make mistakes and need training before the work can be trusted.

lessons.lesson: Look for businesses that already work with human labour, then substitute AI for the labour.
Treat AI as the engine, not the company, and keep tools swappable.
Start small with easy customers to gain experience before aiming at high-value clients.
A productized service capped by one person's hours can scale if AI covers production.
Prepare with current tools instead of waiting for the better model.
Tedious work that people avoid, such as bookkeeping cleanup, is a good opening for outsourced AI.
Regulation or restriction of a technology can signal its importance, but it also brings supply and legal risk.

evidence_quality.rationale: Host solo speculation. The business ideas are untested and rest on second-hand numbers, and the claims about Fable and the government action cannot be verified from this transcript. Transcript quality is Whisper-tiny.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Sponsored GoHighLevel read, a paid community subscription ($5/month) and business plans sold for $19.
